sentence_stem: The new bus is much faster than the old one, so
correct_completion: most people now take it to work.
full_sentence: The new bus is much faster than the old one, so most people now take it to work.
acceptable_variants: many people have started using it.
more people now ride it every day.

options.text: the old bus is more comfortable.
options.why_wrong: 'So' introduces a result of the speed difference, but this option describes comfort, which the stem does not mention.

options.text: most people now take it to work.
the new bus was the slowest of all.
options.why_wrong: This contradicts the stem, which says the new bus is faster, so it cannot be a logical result of that comparison.

options.text: it is more expensive than the train.
options.why_wrong: This adds information about price, which does not follow as a result of the speed comparison started by 'faster than'.

grammar_focus: Comparatives with 'faster than' followed by a result clause with 'so'
explanation: The stem uses a comparative adjective, 'faster than', to compare two buses. The connector 'so' introduces the result of that comparison, so the completion must describe what people do because of the speed. Spanish speakers often place the comparison after the noun or add extra words such as 'más' twice, but English uses only the suffix or 'more' once before the adjective.
translation: El autobús nuevo es mucho más rápido que el antiguo, así que ahora la mayoría de la gente lo usa para ir al trabajo.
